answers.answer: Build three separately shuffled tiers and stack them top to bottom as: 1 randomly dealt Conflict I card, 5 randomly dealt Conflict II cards, then all 4 Conflict III cards in shuffled order. Return all unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup: the final order from top to bottom is 1 Conflict I, 5 Conflict II, all 4 Conflict III; unused Conflict cards are returned to the box without looking.

answers.answer: Each human starts with 2 Agents on their Leader and a third Agent (the Swordmaster) beside the board. They have 12 troops total: 3 in their garrison and 9 in supply. Each takes 1 water and starts with one cube at the bottom of each of the four Influence tracks. Starting VP is 0 in three-player play and 1 in four-player play.
answers.evidence: Setup: each player places 2 Agents on their Leader and sets their third Agent next to the board; the other 12 cubes are troops, 3 in the garrison; each takes 1 water; Score track is 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0; one cube starts at the bottom of each Faction track.

answers.answer: Yes. You may take your Reveal turn while Agents remain. After taking it, your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase, so you cannot take another Agent turn. Plot Intrigue may be played during your own Agent or Reveal turns, but not later after your Reveal turn has ended.
answers.evidence: Agent turns are optional: you may take your Reveal turn while you still have Agents left; once you have taken it, your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase. Plot cards can be played during one of your own Agent or Reveal turns.

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up and use one matching Agent icon to send exactly one Agent to an unoccupied space. A card with no Agent icons cannot be used for an Agent turn. Pay the space's costs and meet its requirements; costs are paid immediately before resolving any space or card effects, and if you cannot pay you cannot send the Agent there. A card cannot send multiple Agents.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: play one card; choose only one Agent icon (one card can't send multiple Agents); no-icon cards can only be revealed; the destination must be unoccupied; pay costs and meet requirements, with costs paid immediately before resolving effects.

answers.answer: No. Conspire's 4-spice entry cost must be paid before resolving the played card's Agent box or any space effects, so a spice gain from that card cannot cover a deficit at entry. Once the entry cost is paid, resolve the board-space effect, the card's Agent box, and the one-space Faction Influence advancement in any order.
answers.evidence: Costs are paid immediately, before resolving any effects of the space or played card; Faction-space Influence, the board space, and Agent box may then be resolved in any order. Conspire costs 4 spice.

answers.answer: You can deploy at most 5 troops: all 3 troops recruited this turn (2 from the space and 1 from the card) plus up to 2 from your garrison. Any recruited troops left undeployed go to your garrison. Rally Troops is not a Combat space, so its recruits normally go to your garrison and cannot be deployed there.
answers.evidence: At a Combat space, deploy any or all troops recruited this turn from any source, plus up to two more from your garrison; undeployed recruits go to the garrison. Rally Troops is not a Combat space, so its troops go to the garrison.

answers.answer: The four steps are: (1) reveal all cards remaining in hand, keeping them separate from cards already played on Agent turns; (2) resolve the Reveal boxes of those newly revealed cards, in any order; (3) set Combat strength; (4) clean up. Reveal boxes on cards played during Agent turns are not used. During cleanup, put all cards in front of you from both Agent and Reveal turns into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn steps: Reveal Cards; Resolve Reveal Effects from cards just revealed, not Agent-turn cards; Set Strength; Clean Up all cards from Agent and Reveal turns into discard.

answers.answer: Yes, you may acquire the replacement card because the Imperium Row is refilled immediately and you may also acquire that replacement if you can afford it. Persuasion from different sources may be pooled for one card, and one source's Persuasion may be split across cards. Unspent Persuasion is lost at the end of the Reveal turn. An acquired card goes to your discard pile and is not used immediately. An Acquire box resolves once at the moment you acquire that card, not when you later play it.
answers.evidence: Acquiring cards: the row refills immediately; after acquiring a card you may acquire its replacement. Persuasion can be pooled or split, cannot be saved, and acquired cards go to discard and are not used right away. Acquire box effects happen at acquisition.

answers.answer: Three troops are worth 6 strength and four revealed swords are worth 4, for a total of 10. If your last deployed troop is removed, your strength becomes 0 and cannot be raised by any means, including swords. For a total over 20, flip the Combat marker to its +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Each troop in the Conflict is worth 2 strength and each revealed sword 1; with no troops in the Conflict strength is 0 and cannot be increased; over 20, flip the marker to +20 and start again from the track's beginning.

answers.answer: Starting with the First Player and proceeding clockwise, each player with at least one troop in the Conflict may play any number of Combat Intrigue cards or pass. Passing once does not bind a player on a later opportunity. Combat resolves after all involved players pass consecutively. A 'when you win a Conflict' card is played only after you have won and before moving to the next phase.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue: First Player then clockwise; players with a troop may play any number or pass; an earlier pass does not require passing again; consecutive passes by all involved resolve combat; win-trigger cards are played after winning, before the next phase.

answers.answer: A and B do not win; each takes the second reward. C and D still compete for the third reward, and since C beats D, C receives it; D gets nothing. A tie for second gives the third reward to each tied player, including in games with fewer than four players. A tie for third yields nothing. A player with 0 strength receives no reward. After rewards, troops return to their owners' supply, not their garrisons.
answers.evidence: A first-place tie means no winner and tied players take the second reward; in a four-player game the other two still compete for third. Tied second gets third reward each, tied third gets nothing, 0 strength gets no reward; troops go to supply.

answers.answer: Normal harvesting happens when an Agent visits a Maker space: Imperial Basin yields 1 base spice, Hagga Basin 2, and The Great Flat 3, plus any bonus spice there (Imperial Basin's controller also gains 1 spice). In Phase 4: Makers, after Combat, each of those three spaces with no Agent receives 1 spice from the bank as bonus spice, added to any accumulated bonus. If an Agent moved away before Phase 4 and the space is empty then, it receives the bonus spice.
answers.evidence: Maker spaces are The Great Flat, Hagga Basin, Imperial Basin; in Phase 4 an empty space gets 1 bonus spice. Space effects list base harvests, and the ruling says a Maker space emptied by an Agent moving away still accumulates spice in Phase 4.

answers.answer: Reaching 10 VP mid-round does not end play immediately: the game end is checked at the end of the round in Phase 5. Revealing the last Conflict empties the Conflict Deck, which also triggers the endgame check at the end of that round. Players first resolve any Endgame Intrigue cards, then the player with the most VP wins. Tiebreak order is spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops, then the player who most recently took a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Recall checks 10 or more VP or an empty Conflict Deck; scoring says this is at the end of a round, then Endgame Intrigue cards resolve before winner determination. Tiebreakers list spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops, most recent Reveal turn.

answers.answer: The VP for reaching 2 Influence is lost if you drop below 2 and regained if you reach 2 again. The bonus earned at 4 Influence is kept after dropping below 4 and may be earned again by dropping back and re-advancing. The first player to reach 4 takes the Alliance and its VP. A tied holder keeps it when another player merely ties; a player must advance to a higher space to take it.
answers.evidence: Faction Influence: 2 Influence grants a VP, lost below 2 and regained on returning to 2; the 4-Influence track bonus is not returned and can be earned again. Alliance first goes to the first player at 4; merely tying does not take it, while rising higher transfers it.

answers.answer: When you lose 1 Influence from a tie at 5, the two opponents who were tied with you become eligible; because several players are tied, you choose which one takes the Alliance. If you are the only player at 4 and fall to 3, no one else at 4 or higher can take it, so it returns to the board and you lose its VP. The 4-Influence track bonus already earned remains yours.
answers.evidence: If the holder loses Influence while tied with another, the previously tied player takes the Alliance; if several were tied, the holder chooses one. Falling to 3 or less loses the token; if no player has 4 or more it returns to the board. The track bonus is kept after dropping below 4.

answers.answer: A discard instruction means a card from your hand unless stated otherwise, and the card goes to your discard pile. Trashing permanently removes a card from your hand, discard pile, or in-play area to the game box; a trashed Reserve card returns to its Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless it pays a cost or a card directs you to trash itself. You cannot reshuffle early just to inspect the top card of an empty deck; reshuffle only when unable to draw because the deck is empty.
answers.evidence: Discard means a hand card unless otherwise specified and goes to discard. Trash can remove from hand, discard pile, or in play; Reserve cards return to their Reserve stack; trash is optional except for costs or self-trash directions. Deck exhaustion says reshuffle when unable to draw and cannot reshuffle early to inspect.

answers.answer: While a player controls Arrakeen or Carthag, that controller gains 1 Solari whenever any player, including the controller, sends an Agent there. Imperial Basin's controller gains 1 spice whenever any player visits it. Winning the corresponding Conflict places your Control marker on that space's flag, replacing an opponent's marker. Later, when a Conflict for a space you already control is revealed, you may deploy one troop from your supply to the Conflict.
answers.evidence: Control: winning a Conflict for Arrakeen, Carthag, or Imperial Basin places the marker, replacing an opponent's; controller gets the listed bonus whenever any player visits; on a later matching Conflict reveal, may deploy one troop from supply.

answers.answer: For the Rival, choose an unused color, put one cube at the bottom of each of the four Influence tracks, put remaining cubes in its supply, and leave its garrison without troops. Remove the three Arrakeen cards marked 1P, shuffle the remaining House Hagal deck, and place it with the Rival's three Agents near its supply; there is no Rival Leader or solo difficulty setup. After each First Player Agent turn, it takes one Agent turn if it has an Agent in supply; it does not act after the other human's turn or a Reveal turn. Its Agents are recalled to supply each round. It never Reveals. It does not collect resources, build an Imperium deck, earn Conflict rewards or VP, or claim Control, but it can take and hold Faction Alliances.
answers.evidence: House Hagal setup specifies unused color, cubes, no garrison troops, removal of three 1P Arrakeen cards, remaining shuffled cards and three Agents. It acts after each First Player Agent turn, never Reveals, and can hold Alliances but does not earn VP/rewards or claim Control.

answers.answer: If the indicated space is occupied, keep revealing House Hagal cards until an eligible unoccupied space appears. Reshuffle immediately if the deck is empty or a Reshuffle card appears, then continue revealing. Ignore normal space costs, requirements, and effects; resolve only the card's icons and instructions. Each troop icon recruits from its supply and is deployed if this is a Combat space, otherwise placed in its garrison; whenever Hagal sends an Agent to a Combat space, it may also deploy up to two garrison troops even if it recruited none. Harvest Spice follows the card instructions, and harvested bonus spice is removed from the space and returned to the bank. If a two-space card's applicable option is occupied, draw a new card; do not switch to its other option.
answers.evidence: House Hagal: occupied spaces prompt further reveals; reshuffle on empty deck or Reshuffle card; ignore ordinary space costs, requirements and effects; recruit/deploy as specified; deploy up to two garrison troops at Combat spaces; Harvest Spice removes harvested bonus to bank; a blocked applicable option means draw again, never switch.

answers.answer: At the start of Combat, if Hagal has at least one troop in the Conflict, reveal a Hagal card and add only its sword icons to Hagal's normal 2 strength per deployed troop. Humans may play Combat Intrigue cards before Combat resolves. Hagal receives no reward for its rank but occupies that rank when human rewards are assigned. If it wins a Conflict for a space a human controls, remove that human's Control marker; Hagal does not replace it. Ordinary third place pays nothing, but a tie for second pays the third reward to each tied human, even in a two-player game.
answers.evidence: House Hagal Combat: reveal a card if it has troops; add sword icons to 2 strength per deployed troop; humans then may play Combat Intrigue. Hagal gets no reward but occupies its rank; winning a controlled space removes the human marker; ordinary third place is nothing while second-place ties get third reward each.
